Prior review retained below:
Distinct review after drafting revisited all 240 question-level rationales, all 15 briefs and counterevidence, agreement wording, institutional scope, neutral/unknown distinctions, current incumbent and policy dates. Corrected the local-government handbook link to the verified 2019 edition, removed unsupported exact publication dates, replaced hospital ownership evidence with the direct medical-institutions survey, confirmed flag-law commencement on 13 August 2026 and added its lawful-expression qualification, and updated imperial-ritual evidence to the 2018 government explanation and 2019 implementation account. Rechecked the Naha judgment and religious tax treatment directly. Kept 14 precise unknowns: authority-liberty-06; progressive-traditionalist-10; innovation-caution-07,08,11; culture-nature-02,05,06,09,10,11,12,13,14. Culture/Nature judgments are limited institutional inferences from adopted guidance, not attributions based on government-funded studies. In particular, attention guidance about sleep, school moral teaching, antidiscrimination law and nationality crime counts were judged insufficient for their separate comparative-causation questions. Incumbent reshuffle verified from 17 September 2026 official record; later operative tax/immigration provisions excluded. Commons File page and local PNG visually checked (960×640, 5194 bytes). The five social-policy neutral answers were reviewed individually: changes vary by institution; recognition differs by family status; abortion permission has legal restrictions; national lessons coexist with parental engagement; education combines inheritance and independent judgement. Parent retains independent audit, shared image credit integration and any eventual publication. Validation blocks publication for the unresolved answers; no scores or neighbour comparisons are available. Separate completion review: challenged all new estimates against the exact wording and earlier gap reasons. Assumptions remain contextual extrapolations, not verified implemented rules or causal rankings. Specific restrictions: nonsuspect records versus document schedules; public dress versus school accommodations; healthy implanted enhancement versus therapeutic/noninvasive products; interests versus career choices; individual heredity versus national/racial causes; immediate intuition versus reflective education. Neither a modifiable trait nor a funded study proves predominance or adoption. Mixed responses reflect an affirmative interaction or conditional-policy interpretation rather than uncertainty alone. New assumption IDs: authority-liberty-06, progressive-traditionalist-10, innovation-caution-07, innovation-caution-08, innovation-caution-11, culture-nature-02, culture-nature-05, culture-nature-06, culture-nature-09, culture-nature-10, culture-nature-11, culture-nature-12, culture-nature-13, culture-nature-14. Prior complete same-agent assessment review is retained; this continuation does not claim a fresh independent 240-source reread or human sign-off. Shared credits and validation are recorded in the completion report. Completion validator warnings were read individually: neutral choices reflect mixed ownership, service-specific contracting, staged/graded regulation, family-law distinctions or explicit development interaction. No neighbour reached 95% in the saved pre-archive diagnostics; archive revalidates against added peers.

neutralAnswers.rationale: Educated assumption: Institutional inference: Public-interest reporting using lawful methods is protected, while unauthorised disclosure and acquisition of designated secrets can be punished. Protection is conditional, not a blanket misconduct-publication immunity. Most likely Neutral. The cited facts provide contextual evidence for an institutional estimate, not a verified explicit national endorsement of this exact statement. Implemented safeguards and exceptions may differ across jurisdictions and cases; the exact normative permission is inferred from the cited controls and rights.
